title: Run credential call
description: The body of the control plane's call with the path run-credential, a POST of application/json to the adapter's call_url followed by run-credential (adapter.schema.json), signed as definitions.schema.json describes a call: an access credential for one run, for the resources, at the access level access, for the purpose purpose, under one grant: for a call whose purpose is harness, the grant grant_ref; for a call whose purpose is work, which has no grant_ref, a grant of the connection of the live collection whose ref is the one resource, the grant that covers that collection, and never a grant of another connection (a ref is unique among the integration's live collections, source-collections.schema.json). For a call whose purpose is harness, grant_ref and each resource are as the adapter answered them to a resolve call (resolve-answer.schema.json). The adapter answers a signed 200 with run-credential-answer.schema.json, or refuses with refusal.schema.json, in this order: 409 grant_unknown, for a call with grant_ref, the adapter holds no grant grant_ref; 403 resource_not_covered, the grant does not cover one of the resources, or, for a call whose purpose is work, no live collection has the one resource as its ref, or no grant of that collection's connection covers it; 403 access_not_granted, the grant does not allow access for the resources, such as write under a grant that allows read alone; 503 source_unavailable, the source did not answer or was busy, and the control plane may send the call again later, built anew. How far one credential reaches is the description's credential_scope (description.schema.json). A call whose purpose is work has exactly one resource in resources, the ref of the collection of the run's target, exactly as the adapter wrote it as ref in its listing of collections (source-collections.schema.json) and as collection_ref in its listing of items (source-items.schema.json); when the run's target came from an item, that collection is the item's collection. That resource is not a resource_ref of a resolve result. A call whose purpose is work has one resource because the answer stays inside the run's work credential entry, whose paths the control plane fills with the path of that one target (run-credential-answer.schema.json); a call whose purpose is harness has 1 to 64. The adapter refuses a call whose time is more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. The adapter has one access key for every organisation, and no call contains a connection_id, so a resolve result can contain a grant_ref of a connection of another organisation. The control plane uses a resolve result only under a grant that the run may use: a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation; or, only to read a harness source and only with access read, a grant whose organisation assigned that source to the run's organisation, at that version and at that path or export. Under an assignment, the control plane sends a call with the path run-credential only when the credential_scope of the adapter's description is resource, which it also is when absent (description.schema.json), and with resources set to the resource_ref of the assigned source alone; when credential_scope is grant, the control plane sends no call with the path run-credential under an assignment, and reads the assigned source only with the call with the path read. A harness source is a remote source that the run's harness extends or takes a module from, whether that harness is the harness file of the target or the harness member of the run documents (run/v1 documents.schema.json). An assignment never covers a call with the path run-credential whose purpose is work or whose access is write: work access comes only from a grant of a live connection of the run's organisation. The control plane treats every other resolve result as covered: false, so nothing that a run of one organisation receives shows that another organisation holds a grant for that address. The control plane sends the calls with the paths run-credential and read only under a grant that the run may use. An access token covers its resources at every version and at every path, so an assignment of one version and one path or export still lets the run read the whole resource with the access token. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The adapter refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the control plane built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The adapter refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

grant_ref.description: The grant the credential is minted under, as the adapter reported it (grant.schema.json). Present exactly when the purpose is harness. A call whose purpose is work has no grant_ref: the adapter uses a grant of the connection of the live collection whose ref is the one resource, the grant that covers that collection, and never a grant of another connection.

resources.description: The resources the credential covers, none twice. For the purpose harness, 1 to 64, each a resource_ref as the adapter answered it to a resolve call. For the purpose work, exactly one: the ref of the collection of the run's target, exactly as the adapter wrote it as ref in its listing of collections (source-collections.schema.json) and as collection_ref in its listing of items (source-items.schema.json); when the run's target came from an item, that collection is the item's collection.

access.description: read, or write: the access level the run has on the resources, the access of the run's documents (run/v1 documents.schema.json).

purpose.description: harness, a credential the run uses to fetch what composes its harness; or work, a credential the run uses for its work on the resources.
